STR profiles of patient-derived models from JAX and the NCI PDMR

Source: R/data.R
pdxSTRProfiles.Rd

Reference STR profiles for 1,258 patient-derived models: 435 from The Jackson Laboratory PDX program and 823 from the NCI Patient-Derived Models Repository (PDMR). This is the default database of STRprofilerApp(), and can be passed as the reference of compareProfiles() or scoreProfiles() to check models against it.

Usage

data(pdxSTRProfiles)

Format

A STRProfiles object of 1,258 samples typed at 18 markers: amelogenin and 17 autosomal STRs (the 13 CODIS core loci plus D2S1338, D19S433, Penta D, and Penta E). sampleData() holds

Center

Source of the model, "JAX" or "PDMR".

Passage

Passage of the profiled material, where recorded.

nDroppedCalls

Calls dropped at ingest as not being alleles (see readSTRProfiles()).

Source

Profiles provided by The Jackson Laboratory PDX program and the NCI PDMR, as compiled for the default database of the strprofiler Python package (0.5.1, strprofiler/shiny_app/www/main_database.csv), and redistributed here under the package's MIT license. See inst/scripts/README.md.

Details

Built by inst/scripts/make-pdxSTRProfiles.R, which reads inst/extdata/main_database.csv with readSTRProfiles() defaults. The raw file is kept alongside, as an example of a database file with metadata columns:

system.file("extdata", "main_database.csv", package = "STRprofilerR")

Twenty-two samples each carry one call that is not an allele (mostly OL, off-ladder), dropped at ingest and counted in nDroppedCalls.

References

Andrews JM, Lloyd MW, Neuhauser SB, Bundy M, Jocoy EL, Airhart SD, Bult CJ, Evrard YA, Chuang JH, Baker S (2024). STRprofiler: efficient comparisons of short tandem repeat profiles for biomedical model authentication. Bioinformatics, btae713. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae713 .

Examples

data(pdxSTRProfiles)
pdxSTRProfiles
#> class: STRProfiles
#> samples(1258): J000077451 J000077591 ... K98450 SA0426
#> markers(18): Amelogenin CSF1PO ... PentaE PentaD
#> sampleData(3): Center Passage nDroppedCalls
#> markerClass: amelogenin(1) autosomal(17)
#> source(1): main_database.csv
table(sampleData(pdxSTRProfiles)$Center)
#> 
#>  JAX PDMR 
#>  435  823 

# Check a batch of models against it.
batch <- readSTRProfiles(
    system.file("extdata", "Example_Batch_File.csv", package = "STRprofilerR")
)
cmp <- compareProfiles(batch, pdxSTRProfiles)
summary(cmp)[, c("Sample", "mixed", "topHit")]
#> DataFrame with 3 rows and 3 columns
#>               Sample     mixed             topHit
#>          <character> <logical>        <character>
#> Sample_A    Sample_A     FALSE J000077451: 100.00
#> Sample_B    Sample_B     FALSE  J000077960: 85.71
#> Sample_C    Sample_C     FALSE J000078366: 100.00
